shapes.shape: (1) Connect monday to a customer's other systems (CRM, ERP, ticketing) via MCP or APIs
shapes.why: Nothing published evaluates an integration end to end. Sensei adapters are text-in/text-out (http, stdio, openai-compat, langserve), so tool calls, arguments and side effects on the CRM/ERP/ticketing side are never observed. The mondaycom/mcp repo has about 84 Jest files, all mock-based (createMockApiClient), with no live-account or LLM-in-the-loop tests and no tool-selection benchmark. The one agent eval found (agentic-monday) scores skill-trigger routing, 13/13 on 13 author-written prompts, not task success. The failures that bite an integration only show up live and cross-model: issue #501 (failed writes returned as success, no isError), #496 (relation, mirror and dependency column writes look failed but succeed, which invites duplicate retries), #508 (search tool with 8 required fields breaks GPT-5.5 in Copilot Studio), #218 (board-info output eats context). Daily API caps (Enterprise 25,000, Pro 10,000) are a scaling constraint no suite exercises. Usable as-is: mock unit tests as tool-contract smoke checks, and the GraphQL codegen drift check. ARCS plug: score tool-call traces plus a deterministic before/after board-state diff against a golden end state, add read-after-write checks and idempotency or dedupe-ledger probes, inject faults (429, partial write, stale ID), and keep it Kintsugi-style so an isError miss is shown, not patched. These are proposals, not built.

shapes.shape: (2) Agents that execute work (SDR qualification, support triage, reporting) and must be qualified before deployment
shapes.why: This is the shape Sensei was built for, and it is the only one with a named suite: sdr-qualification (3 execution scenarios, 1 reasoning, 1 self-improvement), customer-support (same shape), content-writer. Usable as a smoke gate, not as qualification. (a) Fixtures are merged into the agent's context but the judge only sees the prompt string (inputContext is always '{}'), so personalization and pain-point-extraction are rated on plausibility, not accuracy. A fluent fabrication scores like a grounded answer. (b) KPIs are nearly all LLM-judge rubrics from one gpt-4o call at temp 0; the only automated check is an all-or-nothing word-count. There is no ground truth, such as BANT fields against labels or triage category against a human label, so predictive validity is untested. (c) n=1 to 3 scenarios per layer, one run, no variance or pass^k, with gold/silver/bronze cut at 90/75/60 inside plausible noise. (d) The badge averages, so a catastrophic failure can be laundered by the weighted mean, and a judge outage becomes a KPI score of 0 rather than a failed run. (e) Support has no fixtures (only SDR has them), there is no triage or reporting suite, and the README's QA, Data Analysis and Developer suites do not exist. (f) The repo is dormant since 2026-03-22 at v0.0.3, and its history looks AI-built and adopted (inferred), so it is not a monday-validated standard. ARCS plug: per-KPI receipts carrying the evidence quote and a confidence that is actually used, ground-truth calibration reported as sufficiency=insufficient with n when labelled cases are few (Accountant pattern), a Loki-style skeptic pass on the judge, hard-fail gates (Y-gate RED) on safety and write-correctness KPIs. Caveat: ARCS's own outcome closure is 2 of 247, so calibration is a design claim, not a proven one.

shapes.shape: (3) Governed AI in regulated or cautious enterprises (permissions, audit trail, change control, one-way-door approvals)
shapes.why: No published eval touches governance, and the platform itself has stated holes. monday's MCP security page says self-service export of detailed MCP/API audit logs is not available and that audit/telemetry (OWASP MCP08) is internal only; the audit_logs GraphQL query (Enterprise plus manage_account_security) covers security events and the docs do not say it records per-tool MCP calls. Prompt-injection and output validation are assigned to the customer or AI client, and the repo has no untrusted-content wrapping, tagging or sanitisation of data returned to the model; the only injection-related test checks tool descriptions for ';' and backticks. Read-only mode is a registration-time filter on each tool's self-declared type (submit_bug_or_feature_request is typed READ), not a permission check, and it lives only in the open stdio layer; the hosted server source is not public. --mode apps can set app env vars and promote an app to live with a personal token. Scopes are coarse with no per-board scope. ATP offers approval pause/resume (fails closed with no handler), provenance policies and tool rules, but provenance defaults to off, the default JWT secret is hard-coded when unset, and the repo ships security e2e tests but no published injection benchmark. Sensei has no safety layer, and a downloaded marketplace suite can spawn arbitrary processes via the stdio adapter, with no signing seen. ARCS plug: an indirect-injection scenario pack on the customer's own boards scored on obedience, a gateway-side audit sink (who, prompt, tool, args, result, ticket id), and ARCS WRITE-LOCK as a testable gate so one-way-door tools (promote_app, set_environment_variable, bulk delete) require a declared lock. Proposals only.

shapes.shape: (4) Adoption and ROI measurement after launch
shapes.why: Sensei is a pre-deployment, single-run qualification harness, so it has no post-launch telemetry: no drift or regression tracking over time, no run-id or seed in results, no outcome KPIs, no link from a score to a business metric. The only per-caller usage visibility monday documents is the API analytics dashboard (usage, trends, top contributors), available to admins with the API usage add-on and to Enterprise; that is call volume, not task success, adoption quality or ROI, and MCP calls are not separately attributed in the docs (inferred). Gateway pricing, rate limits and token rates for monday AI tokens were not found. The nearest public hint of outcome tracking is the user-run feedback tool and the open-issue stream, which are product feedback, not customer ROI. ARCS plug: the Accountant pattern (closed-position rates and NCI-vs-outcome calibration only when n>=30 per cohort, else sufficiency=insufficient) and receipt history across runs for drift. Caveat: ARCS capture is the weak point (2 of 247 receipts closed), so pitch it as the discipline, not a proven result.

shapes.shape: (5) Data and PII constraints that force private or local models
shapes.why: The harness is plausibly runnable offline, but nothing is shown, and nothing evaluates PII handling. Judge config takes a base_url and the openai-compat agent adapter defaults to 127.0.0.1:18789, so pointing both at Ollama or vLLM should work with no code change (inferred, not demonstrated in the repo). Weak points: the CLI defaults to gpt-4o as judge; the Anthropic provider throws unless fronted by an OpenAI-compatible proxy; the judge demands JSON-only output with 2-3 sentence reasoning, which small open-weights judges often break, and a parse failure becomes a score of 0; marketplace install/search/publish phones home to sensei.sh, so air-gapped use must stay on local suites. monday-hosted AI routes to OpenAI and Anthropic only, with BYO model unsupported per monday's FAQ (inferred from search summaries; the gateway page states no data-handling terms). No official monday Hugging Face org, models, datasets or Spaces exist (HF API 404 and empty author listings for five name variants), and no HF usage appears in mondaycom code (code search can miss). The only open-weights reference is qwen2.5-coder:7b via Ollama in ATP's e2e test config, a test fixture, not a product feature. No PII-leak, redaction or data-residency KPI exists anywhere. ARCS plug: run the same suite with a local judge and a local agent, record judge model and prompt hash in the receipt, add PII canary scenarios (planted identifiers that must not appear in outputs or logs) and a judge-agreement check before a small local judge is trusted. Proposals only.

shapes.shape: (6) Comparing models or agents for a specific workflow (hosted frontier vs open weights)
shapes.why: Because Sensei targets any text endpoint, the same YAML suite can be pointed at several agents, so a side-by-side is mechanically possible. It is not statistically defensible. One run per agent, no repeated trials, intervals or pass^k, so differences smaller than run-to-run noise look like winners. Same-family judge bias is unmitigated (the judge can share a family with one contender; no order randomisation, length control or cross-model judge), and the judge's own confidence output is collected and never used. No cost, latency or token accounting beyond openai-compat usage.total_tokens, which matters for hosted vs open-weights tradeoffs. Tool-using or MCP agents can be compared only on final text, not tool choice or outcome. The judge cannot see fixtures, so accuracy differences between a frontier model and a smaller open model are invisible when both write fluent text. multi_judge and scenario pools exist in the engine but are unreachable from the CLI and unused by shipped suites, and the result JSON lacks seed, run id and prompt hashes, so comparisons are not reproducible. ARCS plug: k trials per scenario with bootstrapped intervals, a cross-family and position-swapped judge, a ground-truth-first scorer with the judge reserved for residue, cost and latency in every receipt, and a FORK/PARADOX Y-state when the intervals overlap instead of a forced winner. Proposals only.

shapes.shape: (7) Turning one-off deployments into reusable assets and feeding evidence back to product
shapes.why: Distribution plumbing exists, evidence plumbing does not. Reusable assets: Sensei suites as YAML with marketplace slug, tags and install/search/publish; mondaycom/skills (5 Agent Skills) and the near-duplicate cowork plugin; the agentic-monday plugin marketplace (monday-api, monday-code, vibe) with docs on rate limits, pagination, error taxonomy and column types; the mcp repo's Gemini, Claude and Cursor plugin dirs and MCP registry entry; ATP examples; the @vibe/mcp server that stops agents inventing UI. Feedback to product: public issue tracker (53 open on mcp, many external) and a submit_bug_or_feature_request tool. Weak points: the skills carry no evals or tests, and the single eval file has no visible CI; the Sensei registry server and any certification authority are not in the repo and badges are a computed string with no signature; results lack run id, seed, judge-prompt version and cost, so a customer's score cannot be compared or aggregated across deployments; agentic-monday's monday-code .mcp.json needs a hand-edited token placeholder; README tool tables are stale (about 14 of 90 or more tools); the sensei README roadmap and suite claims have drifted from the code. ARCS plug: every deployment ends with a receipt (what_confirmed vs what_unconfirmed, refs) and each reusable skill or suite gets a falsification pass before promotion, which turns FDE field evidence into a structured, provenance-tagged product-feedback record. Proposals only.

shapes.shape: (8) Long-horizon multi-step workflows with human checkpoints
shapes.why: No published eval samples long-horizon structure. Every Sensei suite is 1 to 3 single-shot execution scenarios plus one reasoning and one self-improvement scenario; depends_on is a single hop that prepends 'Previous output:' text to a fresh prompt; adapters are stateless per call; there are no multi-turn episodes, environment state, delayed reward, step or budget limits, or recovery scoring. The reasoning layer is a post-hoc 'explain your approach' prompt, so explanation faithfulness cannot be tested without traces. Self-improvement is a static feedback string, so it measures revision prompt-following, not learning or retention. Human checkpoints exist as runtime features, not as something evaluated: ATP atp.approval.request pauses execution, returns control to the client and resumes within maxPauseDuration (default 1h) with the same clientId and token, failing closed when no handler is configured, and the default in-memory cache needs Redis for multi-pod resume. Nothing scores whether the agent asks at the right moment, resumes correctly or avoids acting before approval. monday's rate limits (daily, minute, concurrency, complexity) make partial writes and mid-run cap exhaustion realistic, and none are modelled. ARCS plug: Golden Inchworm style multi-pass episodes in a sandbox monday account with injected faults, checkpoint-correctness KPIs (asked when stakes warranted, did not act before approval, resumed with state intact), pass^k over episodes, and WRITE-LOCK declaration checked as a precondition for one-way-door steps. Proposals only; not built.

plugs.shape: (1) Connect monday to a customer's other systems (CRM, ERP, ticketing) via MCP or APIs
plugs.arcs_primitive: Trace-and-ledger discipline, not an integration eval. (a) operators/ledger/operator-receipts.jsonl, the append-only per-call ledger the MCP bridge writes, is the model for recording tool, args, result. (b) arcs-verb-eval Assessment (claim against record, verdict per claim) is the model for diffing a golden end state against the real board state. (c) operators/arcs_kintsugi.py is the 'show the break, no silent patch' rule for a failed write that returned success (monday/mcp #501). ARCS has no monday client, no sandbox account, and no tool-call tracer for third-party MCP servers.
plugs.status: partial: the ledger and the Assessment verdict are built, the ledger covers ARCS operator calls only, and the integration eval itself is not built. Fault injection, read-after-write and board-state diff: not built
plugs.to_build: A harness that drives an agent against a sandbox monday account through the real MCP server and captures every tool call and argument. A deterministic before/after board-state diff against a golden end state (a rules-lane gate in the arcs-verb-eval style, stdlib only). Read-after-write checks for the #496 relation/mirror/dependency columns. An idempotency probe that retries a write and counts duplicates. A fault injector for 429, partial write and stale ID. An isError/success-mismatch scorer for #501. Exercise the daily API cap. Use the existing mock-based mondaycom/mcp tests as a smoke tier underneath rather than rewriting them.

plugs.shape: (2) Agents that execute work (SDR qualification, support triage, reporting) and must be qualified before deployment
plugs.arcs_primitive: Ground-truth-first scoring with the judge as residue. (a) operators/arcs_accountant.py (Operator 19): reports sufficiency=insufficient with n when too few closed positions, calibrates only at n>=30 closed per cohort, never defaults a missing field; its self-test proves both refusals. Adapter: operators/prod_receipt_to_accountant.py; weekly wrapper scripts/accountant_weekly.py. (b) tools/arcs-verb-eval/arcs_verb_eval_judge.py: the LLM judge scores a 0-2 rubric but cannot change a gate or the fate, and every call logs prompt, model and tokens in the trace. (c) tools/arcs-verb-eval/arcs_verb_eval_lenses.py: at stakes:high a gauntlet must carry five lenses and at least one dissent, and the step fails closed. (d) scripts/provenance_lint.py: any quantified claim without a ledger entry fails, which is the missing 'is the personalization grounded in the fixture' check in spirit. (e) src/lib/ygate.ts: a RED/hard-fail state for KPIs that must not average out.
plugs.status: partial: mechanical gates built and used on ARCS's own artifacts; the Accountant is built but its calibration is unproven (outcome capture is low, AGENTS.md records 2 of 247 receipts closed; the Accountant docstring notes a 2026-09-24 cohort correction to that framing, so cite it as 'low' and not as a precise rate). Nothing here has been run against a monday agent or a labelled SDR/triage set
plugs.to_build: A labelled-case harness (BANT fields vs labels, triage category vs a human label) that feeds the fixtures into the judge AND the agent, reusing existing contains/regex/json-schema checks in Sensei rather than inventing new primitives. A per-KPI receipt carrying the evidence quote and a confidence that is actually consumed. k trials per scenario with pass^k and no weighted-mean laundering, plus hard-fail KPIs for safety and write-correctness. A judge outage must fail the run instead of scoring 0. A skeptic pass on the judge, modelled on the lens dissent requirement.
